blocks.explanation:
A proof. The left side is an A.G.P.: A.P. part \(1, 2, 3, \ldots\), G.P. ratio \(1 + \frac1n\).
Calling the ratio \(y\) keeps it short, and \(1 - y = -\frac1n\) is very simple.
Plan: put \(y = 1 + \frac1n\), multiply by \(y\), shift, subtract, sum the G.P., simplify to \(n^2\).
steps:
Given: \(1 + 2y + 3y^{2} + \cdots + n\,y^{n-1}\) with \(y = 1 + \frac1n\)
To find: prove the sum is \(n^2\).
Method: Multiply-by-\(r\)-and-subtract (the method of 6.8.1): write \(S_n\), write \(rS_n\) one place to the right, subtract; the middle becomes a G.P. that we can sum. Here \(\frac{1}{1 - y} = -n\).

Introduce \(y\)
\[y = 1 + \dfrac{1}{n}\]
\[1 - y = -\dfrac{1}{n}\]
\[\dfrac{1}{1 - y} = -n\]
Why: The \(k\)th term is \(k\,y^{k-1}\), so the \(n\)th (last) term is \(n\,y^{n-1}\).

Write \(S\) and \(yS\)
\[S = 1 + 2y + 3y^{2} + \cdots + n\,y^{n-1}\]
\[yS = y + 2y^{2} + \cdots\]
\[\quad + (n - 1)y^{n-1} + n\,y^{n}\]
Why: Multiply by \(y\) and shift so equal powers line up.

Subtract
\[(1 - y)S = 1 + y + y^{2} + \cdots\]
\[\quad + y^{n-1} - n\,y^{n}\]
Why: Each pair leaves 1 times the power, e.g. \((2 - 1)y = y\); the first term 1 stays; the last term \(ny^n\) is subtracted.

Sum the G.P. and simplify
\[1 + y + \cdots + y^{n-1} = \dfrac{1 - y^{n}}{1 - y}\]
\[= -n(1 - y^{n})\]
\[(1 - y)S = -n + n\,y^{n} - n\,y^{n}\]
\[= -n\]
Why: G.P. with first term 1, ratio \(y\), \(n\) terms; \(\frac{1}{1 - y} = -n\); the \(y^n\) terms cancel.

Find \(S\)
\[S = \dfrac{-n}{1 - y} = (-n)(-n)\]
\[= n^{2}\]
Why: Divide by \(1 - y\), i.e. multiply by \(\frac{1}{1 - y} = -n\).

Check with \(n = 2\)
\[y = \tfrac{3}{2}:\ 1 + 2 \cdot \tfrac{3}{2} = 4 = 2^{2} \;\checkmark\]
Why: Two terms give 4, as the formula says.
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: the sum of \(n\) terms is \(n^{2}\).
